questions.question: Describe on microwave cooking.
questions.solution_html:
• Microwave cooking is a method of cooking food using electromagnetic waves from a power
  • source magnetron.
  • It works on dielectric heating, where polar molecules (mainly water) vibrate rapidly when
  • exposed to microwaves, producing heat.
  • Heat is produced inside the food, unlike conventional cooking w here heat moves from outside to
  • inside.
  • The efficiency of microwave cookery depends upon the constituents of food being cooked.
  • Water in food converts microwaves to heat energy very efficiently followed by starch, cellulose
  • and protein. Least effective is fatty tissues.
  • Only microwave-safe materials like glass, ceramic, and certain plastics can be used; metals reflect
  • microwaves.(1 mark for each point)

questions.question: Explain the components and steps in standardization.
questions.solution_html:
• Recipe Title ( 1 mark)
  • The title should be clear, descriptive, and appealing, highlighting key ingredients or a unique feature of the dish.
  • For example, instead of "Dal," use "Authentic Punjabi Dal Tadka."
  • Recipe Category (1/2 mark)
  • Classifying recipes (main course, side dish, dessert, snack) helps organize menus and plan meals efficiently. For
  • example, "Vegetable Biryani" is a main course, while "Cucumber Raita" is a side dish.
  • Ingredients List (1/2 mark)
  • List ingredients in order of use with exact names, form, and preparation method for consistency. For example
  • "250 g paneer, crumbled" or "1 tbsp cumin seeds, roasted."
  • Weight/Volume of Ingredients (1/2 mark)
  • Use precise standard units like grams or milliliters to ensure accuracy and consistency. For example, "500 g
  • wheat flour" instead of "one bowl of flour."
  • Preparation Instructions (1/2 mark)
  • Provide clear, step-by-step instructions including techniques and pre-preparation steps. For example, "Marinate
  • chicken with yogurt and spices for 4 hours before grilling."
  • Cooking Temperature and Time (1/2 mark)
  • Mention exact temperature and duration to ensure proper cooking and safety. For example, "Bake at 180°C for
  • 25 minutes until golden brown."
  • Serving Size (1/2 mark)
  • Define portion size clearly for consistency and nutrition control. For example, "One serving = 200 g dal with
  • 150 g rice."
  • Recipe Yield (1/2 mark)
  • State the total output in servings or quantity to help scaling and planning. For example, "Yields 10 servings of
  • 250 g each."
  • Equipment and Utensils (1/2 mark)
  • List required tools and their size/type to ensure proper preparation. For example, "Use a 12 -inch skillet and a 4
  • L mixing bowl."
  • Essay Questions
questions.final_answer: Essay Questions
